label: Every framework
summary: What every framework's onboarding settles first: why the organisation takes it on, whether and where it applies, what is in scope, what already exists and who owns it. Nothing here asks for the work of the framework itself (policies, risk assessments, evidence): that starts after onboarding.

source.ref: Scoping practice of certification bodies, regulators and assessors: purpose, starting point and target date come before any assessment

fields.label: Objective
fields.note: Why the organisation takes this framework on. A certification, a regulator's requirement and an internal assessment follow different workflows afterwards.

fields.label: Starting point
fields.note: Whether this is the first implementation, work that is already running, or a move from another tool.

fields.label: Target date
fields.note: The audit, certification or regulatory date to work towards, if there is one.

fields.label: Required by
fields.note: The regulator or customer that asks for it.

source.ref: Scoping practice: the legal entity, the countries and whether the framework covers the whole organisation or part of it are the first applicability facts any assessor asks

fields.label: Legal entity
fields.note: The company that implements the framework and whose name appears on the certificate, report or filing.

fields.label: Countries
fields.note: Where that company operates. A country alone does not decide applicability, but it tells which regulators and laws to look at.

fields.label: Applies to
fields.note: Whether the framework covers everything the entity does, or only some departments, processes, systems or locations.

fields.label: Services covered
fields.note: The products or services the framework covers, if only some.

source.ref: Scoping practice: departments, processes, systems, locations, third parties and justified exclusions define the boundary an assessor tests

fields.label: Departments
fields.note: Departments inside the scope, from the department tree in Governance settings.

fields.label: Processes
fields.note: Business processes inside the scope, with who owns each.

fields.label: Systems
fields.note: Systems and applications inside the scope, picked from the asset inventory.

fields.label: Hosting
fields.note: Where the in-scope systems run.

fields.label: Locations
fields.note: Offices, branches or data centres inside the scope, from the sites in the organisation profile.

fields.label: Third parties
fields.note: Vendors and service providers the in-scope services depend on.

fields.label: Exclusions
fields.note: Anything left out of the scope, each with the reason. Leave empty if nothing is excluded.

fields.label: Scope statement
fields.note: A short statement of what is covered, where and for whom, if one is drafted. AI can draft one from what is picked above.

source.ref: Gap analysis practice: what already exists decides where the work starts, so the platform does not begin from zero

fields.label: Already in place
fields.note: Tick what already exists for this framework. Nothing is needed to continue; the platform uses it to avoid starting from zero.

fields.label: Previous system
fields.note: The tool the work is moving from.

source.ref: Programme governance practice: an accountable owner, an approver of scope and applicability decisions and an independent reviewer are named before work is assigned

fields.label: Programme owner
fields.note: The person accountable for this framework programme.

fields.label: Coordinator
fields.note: Who coordinates assessments day to day, if not the owner.

fields.label: Approver
fields.note: Who approves applicability and scope decisions.

fields.label: Control teams
fields.note: Departments that will implement the controls.

fields.label: Independent review
fields.note: Who will review the compliance work independently.

gate.label: The scope names what is covered
gate.hint: Pick the departments, processes, systems or locations that are covered, or choose Whole organisation.

gate.label: Owner and approver are different people
gate.hint: Someone other than the owner approves scope decisions.
